## Purpose
The live composition root for building a runnable agent: `create_runner(agent_id, ctx)` loads the agent spec, composes its full system prompt (guardrails/skills/hooks/constitution/injects/body), resolves its tool set, builds/roots its per-run disk sandbox, and hands construction off to the registry-selected runtime adapter to produce a `DeepAgentRunner`.

## Shape
- `AgentContext` — the per-invocation runtime context dataclass (user request, prior-agent outputs, attached skills/hooks, model, sandbox/run ids, pre-warmed Constitution and MCP tools, per-step injects).
- `create_runner(agent_id, ctx, ...)` — the public entry point the `ExecutionEngine` calls once per agent; separates the per-run *shared* disk sandbox (keyed on `ctx.run_id`) from the per-agent-invocation *unique* checkpoint `thread_id`.
- `_compose_system_prompt` — builds a named-block map and delegates ordering/join to a registry-resolved `PromptAssemblyPolicy` (default order: injects → guardrails → skills → hooks → constitution → prompt body).
- `_compose_injection` / `_compose_injection_no_template` — assembles the od_prototype/od_ppt template/design-system/craft injection block, including a "blank canvas" fallback scaffold when no template was selected.
- `_resolve_runner_tools` / `_resolve_custom_tool_keys` — resolve `spec.tools` names to concrete LangChain tools via the `tool_provider` registry, unioning in any pre-warmed MCP tools.
- `_select_runtime` / `RuntimeBuildContext` — resolves the `AgentRuntimeAdapter` (currently only `langchain_deepagents`) and hands it a bound zero-arg `build` closure so the kernel-side adapter never has to import `app.*` or `create_deep_agent` directly.

## Why this shape
The module is explicitly the one place permitted to import both the kernel (`agents.*`) and app (`app.*`) layers — comments repeatedly flag this as the "composition root" so the ports-and-adapters import-linter boundary (kernel code must not import `app`) is preserved while still letting the concrete `DeepAgentRunner` get built; the runtime-adapter indirection (`_select_runtime`) exists so a future runtime can be swapped in via the capability registry with no change to kernel code (INV-13).
